title: Monday Night Football power outage leaves fans and players in the dark
summary: The lights at Northwest Stadium went out during the third quarter of Monday night’s game between the Cincinnati Bengals and the Washington Commanders, leading to a delay of about four minutes.

image.caption: Players look on after the lights go out during the third quarter of the game between the Cincinnati Bengals and Washington Commanders at Northwest Stadium in Landover, Md., Monday. (Amber Searls/Imagn Images/Reuters)

blocks.text: World·New
The lights at Northwest Stadium went out during the third quarter of Monday night’s game between the Cincinnati Bengals and the Washington Commanders, leading to a delay of about four minutes.
Lights went out during third quarter of Cincinnati-Washington game
Who turned out the lights?

Fans and players were left in the dark Monday when the lights went out at Northwest Stadium during the third quarter of the game between the Cincinnati Bengals and the Washington Commanders, leading to a delay of about four minutes and widespread, albeit temporary, confusion.

The Commanders were in the red zone, trailing 10-7, when the stadium in Landover, Md., went dark. A collective shout emerged from the crowd, referees blew their whistles, and play-by-play announcer Joe Buck observed, "Somebody turned out the lights."
"Somebody leaned against the wall," he joked a moment later.
"We'll see how long this takes to get them back up and running," quipped analyst Troy Aikman, as the two did their best to fill airspace before going to commercial.
The lights in the stadium went out at the beginning of the third quarter of Bengals-Commanders. https://t.co/f3yeTJONCt—espn
The lights returned after a brief official timeout. The crowd roared and Buck exclaimed: "Let there be light!"
The game resumed and in the end, the Commanders won 22-20.
Later in the broadcast, Buck offered up an explanation for the brief outage.
"The official word is that the lighting vendor never disabled the regularly scheduled maintenance for 10 p.m.," he said.
"It’s a weekday thing, and they forgot it was a Monday night game."
Aikman chuckled in response.
Fans had their say online — some calling it unacceptable, and many joking that the lighting vendor was going to be fired.
"Somebody's getting a very awkward phone call from Roger Goodell tomorrow morning," one fan wrote on X, referring to the NFL commissioner.
The lights at Northwest Stadium went out early in the third quarter, interrupting play. (Julia Demaree Nikhinson/The Associated Press)

The Bengals faced another power outage earlier this month during a game in Madrid, which interrupted the game with fewer than two minutes left of play. Neither outage compares to the 2013 Super Bowl blackout that plunged the stadium into darkness for 34 minutes.

Perhaps the most memorable pro sports lights gaffe was in 1988, when a power outage at Boston Garden halted a tie game between the Boston Bruins and Edmonton Oilers in the NHL Stanley Cup final. The game could not resume and fans were sent home.

blocks.text: Two years later, the same two teams would meet again in the 1990 Stanley Cup final and the power went out again during a tie game, once again at Boston Garden.
That time, however, the lights were restored and the Oilers won 3-2 in triple overtime.
